newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks down by lunch on liquidity worries.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks down by lunch on liquidity worries.

text.p: Thai stocks were lower by the lunchbreak on Wednesday as asset quality and liquidity concerns saw continued sales of finance stocks, analysts said.
The SET Index drifted 2.08 points, or 0.42 percent lower, to 491.05. The SET 50 lost 0.06 points, or 0.17 percent, to 34.86. Turnover was 933 million baht, sharply down on recent days.

Existing liquidity and asset quality concerns surrounding the embattled finance sector were compounded by an announcement that Finance One Plc was in talks to reschedule debt repayments to foreign creditors, analysts and traders said.

"Foreign creditors are clearly going to be unnerved by the announcement this morning that Finance One Plc is in talks to reschedule its debt payments," said a senior foreign analyst at a major local broker.
Finance stocks were 5.98 percent lower though broader falls in the market were pared by gains in the more defensive communications and energy stocks.

Government decrees to support the finance sector were too long term and too vague to fundamentally shift sentiment in the finance sector which a senior local executive said on Monday may have non-performing loans at 31.5 percent of total lending.
Tight domestic liquidity is also a concern as interfinance lending market rates have been over 20 percent so far this week, analysts said.

A release of economic data by the central bank on Thursday has heightened investor caution, particularly as the better figures have not yet been leaked as they have been in past months, the foreign analyst said.
Thai Farmers Bank Plc topped the active list dipping 0.50 to 77.50, Phatra Thanakit Plc lost 1.25 to 24.25 and Dhana Siam Plc dipped 1.25 to 13.50.
